marks.gloss_en: 'you may slaughter and eat' -- you have no permission to eat them except from the time of slaughter onward
(entertained) the clause speaks of offspring conceived and born after their [mothers'] redemption
'zachar' -- to include the offspring (= p_brt_zachar_vlad)
'nekeva' -- to include the substitute (= p_brt_nekeva_temura)
from where? as the Sages taught: 'male' to include the offspring, 'female' to include the substitute
'im zachar' -- to include the offspring of blemished animals (= p_brt_im_zachar_baalei_mumin)
'im nekeva' -- to include the substitute of blemished animals (= p_brt_im_nekeva_baalei_mumin)
I have only the offspring of unblemished animals; from where the offspring of blemished ones? when it says 'whether male' -- to include the offspring of blemished animals
גמר בשעריך בשעריך מבכור: as a firstborn is not dedicated for any offering one wishes, so these are not (= p_sheshet_ein_matpisan_lechol_zevach)
Ravina: may one dedicate them for any offering he wishes? Rav Sheshet: one does not dedicate them [so]
תניא כוותיה דרב ששת: ... ואין מתפיסן לכל זבח שירצה
consecrated animals whose permanent blemish preceded their consecration and which were redeemed are obligated in the firstborn [law] and the gifts
סמוך לפדיונן? למימרא דבני פדייה נינהו? -- the wording is replaced: אלא אימא סמוך לפדיון אמן (= p_chanina_samuch_lepidyon_iman)
the West in R' Chanina's name (literal wording): close to their redemption one dedicates them for that same offering
[offspring born] before redemption: one view -- they are consecrated to be offered
Rav Huna: those [born] after redemption -- one gathers them into a chamber and they die
before their redemption one commits me'ila with them; after their redemption one does not

but if their consecration preceded their blemish, or a passing blemish preceded consecration and afterwards a permanent blemish arose, and they were redeemed -- exempt from the firstborn [law] and the gifts
before their redemption one commits me'ila with them; after their redemption one does not
the reisha's 'general rule' comes to include one who slaughters them outside -- that he is exempt
